idea.description: Recent-conditioned SASRec with multi-negative candidate cross-entropy: add an initially inactive, gated recent-history correction to causal SASRec features and train against 32 uniformly sampled alternatives. Compare it with baseline, objective-only and fusion-only variants.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies stale historical interests and broadly plausible associations displacing specific current matches. Recent conditioning directly targets historical interference; multi-competitor training tests whether finer discrimination reduces broad matches at the top. Neither mechanism proves product compatibility, identifies satisfied demand, or guarantees improved recommendations. Electronics’ 14.95% sampled wrong-rank rate motivates the objective comparison; pinned four-category macro validation HR@10 remains the selection criterion. Modest embedding alignment does not justify adding collapse penalties.

Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, evaluation seed 42 and the SASREC_EPOCHS default of 200. Use the existing baseline optimizer, batching, architecture and learning-rate schedule unchanged initially, recording their resolved values. Do not reset the training RNG before each minibatch or validation checkpoint.

For position t, define m_t=1 when sequence[t] is nonpadding and e_t=sqrt(d)*item_emb(sequence[t]), using the same trainable item table as SASRec. idea.pseudocode:
Preregister four variants and budget/checkpoint rules:
  baseline: baseline features and loss
  objective-only: baseline features, 32-negative candidate CE
  fusion-only: fused features, baseline loss
  combined: fused features, 32-negative candidate CE

For each variant and each of the four categories:
  initialize with training seed 42 using the unchanged preprocessed split
  initialize P=I, gate_w=0, gate_b=-1, alpha=0 where fusion is enabled
  for each batch (None, sequence, positive, negative):
    valid = (sequence != 0) AND (positive != 0)
    h = baseline_SASRec(sequence)
    if fusion enabled:
      e = sqrt(d) * item_emb(sequence)
      r = masked_causal_exponential_mean(e, window=5, decay=0.7)
      g = sigmoid(linear(concat(h, r)))
      z = (h + alpha * g * P(r)) * nonpadding_mask
    else:
      z = h
    if objective enabled:
      for each valid position t:
        A = catalog_without_padding - set(sequence[:t+1]) - {positive[t]}
        if A empty: skip position and increment skip counter
        negatives = uniform_draw_with_replacement(A, K=32)
        logits = score(z[t], [positive[t]] + negatives)
        position_loss = cross_entropy(logits, class_index=0)
      loss = mean(position_loss over eligible positions)
    else:
      loss = baseline_loss(z, positive, negative, valid)
    update parameters with baseline optimizer
  at a preregistered checkpoint reached by all four category runs:
    obtain pinned validation HR@10 for every category
    macro = equal_mean(four_category_HR10)
    log checkpoint opportunity, elapsed GPU-seconds and supporting diagnostics
    apply predetermined complete-configuration promotion and tie-break rules

Select the best eligible joint configuration using macro validation HR@10 only.
Serialize architecture and weights; generate working/predict.py with identical fusion.
Verify generated-predictor score parity on public histories.
Run retained diagnostic interfaces using actual fused features and actual item scores.
Report observed validation results and uncertainty only when underlying hits are available.

idea_diagnosis.description: Augment each category’s SASRec scores with a popularity-centered, shrunk last-item transition residual. Retain unchanged SASRec through zero correction weight and explicitly test whether improvements arise from transition information or popularity suppression.
idea_diagnosis.motivation: The supplied qualitative diagnosis suggests broad associations can dilute specific recent matches, but does not prove that greater recency emphasis helps. Transition counts provide an inexpensive complementary signal. Algebra exposes a shortcut: for unobserved pairs, the residual penalizes destination popularity in proportion to source support. Controlled comparisons are therefore necessary before attributing gains to specific transitions.

Count every adjacent nonpadding pair within each user's training history, including repeated transitions; never cross user or category boundaries. Let n_i=sum_j C[i,j]. Define destination popularity over all training interaction occurrences, p[j]=(f[j]+1)/(sum_k f[k]+M), for the M eligible nonpadding items. Fix tau=20 for this initial experiment as an explicit heuristic, not an established optimum. Set r(i,j)=(C[i,j]-n_i*p[j])/(n_i+tau); unseen source rows produce exactly zero correction.

Train the unchanged per-category SASRec with preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and the environment's SASREC_EPOCHS default of 200. Obtain normalization statistics once per category from 10,000 training prefix–candidate pairs sampled with replacement using a separate seed-42 generator: sample uniformly from valid next-item training positions, use their causal prefixes truncated exactly as during training, and draw a uniform nonpadding candidate excluding the prefix and its next target. Skip positions without an eligible candidate and record the resulting count. Compute neural-score population standard deviation and residual root mean square in float64; clamp both at epsilon=1e-8 and serialize them. If the sample is empty, use scales of one and record the missing evidence. Do not normalize over evaluation candidates. Use s/sigma_s + alpha*r/RMS_r; dividing baseline scores by a positive category constant preserves its ordering at alpha=0.

Select a single shared alpha across all four categories from {0,0.25,0.5,0.75,1}, using only pinned macro validation HR@10. Break equal aggregate hit counts by choosing smaller alpha. Preserve the evaluator's tie handling and candidate sets. Save category scores and each user's binary hit for every configuration. Avoid independently selecting category weights: five choices per category would permit 625 combinations. Keep a cumulative configuration ledger across subsequent searches; small searches can still overfit validation.

For exploratory attribution, compare corrections -p[j], -log(p[j]), exact penalty -n_i*p[j]/(n_i+tau), count-only C[i,j]/(n_i+tau), and log-lift log((C[i,j]+tau*p[j])/((n_i+tau)*p[j])). Normalize each correction by its training-sample RMS and independently tune its strength on the same five-value grid. Unobserved log-lift pairs have a destination-independent correction; this avoids the residual's specific popularity penalty but can emphasize rare observed destinations. These controls are separate exploratory analyses, not free additional evidence for the primary selected model. Before claiming transition-specific gains, compare a randomized transition multigraph obtained through endpoint swaps that preserve source and destination totals; record seed, requested swaps, and accepted swaps. A history-aware extension averages corrections over the last five nonpadding items with normalized weights proportional to 0.5^age, age zero being newest. Treat this fixed extension as an additional exploratory configuration, not an established optimum. All computation and failed trials count against the shared budget; prioritize the primary branch and popularity controls before extensions.

Report target-pair support and candidate-pair support separately: for each validation user, target support indicates C[last,target]>0, and candidate support is the fraction of the fixed 100 candidates with positive counts. Report HR@10 changes by transition support, training source-frequency quartiles, target-popularity quartiles, and history-length quartiles, with category-specific bin boundaries derived only from training data, retained duplicate boundaries, and subgroup sizes. Do not treat these strata as additional selection objectives.

Store counts as sorted CSR rows; avoid an M-by-M dense matrix. Candidate scoring gathers sparse counts. Full-catalog scoring uses chunked neural matrix multiplication, initializes the analytic negative-popularity term, and adds sparse observed-edge corrections. Empty histories bypass potentially undefined all-padding neural features and return training popularity; a nonempty history with an unseen transition source receives the neural score alone. Apply the benchmark's existing seen-item exclusions without modifying evaluation.

Provide a shared scorer score(features, items, source_items) for inference and architecture-aware probes. Preserve predict_score(features, items) as the compatible neural-component scorer and explicitly identify its scope in metric definitions; probes measuring deployed scores must call the shared scorer with source IDs. At diagnostic position t, use sequence[:,t] as source for the causal feature predicting positive[:,t]. Mask padding targets and sources, handle B-by-L tensors explicitly, and never infer source IDs from cached features. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). view.model remains the actual trained nn.Module. Run under no_grad, restore the prior training mode in finally, and return metrics, metric_definitions, observation counts, and nulls for unavailable measurements. Distinguish scaled margins from rank-based evidence.

Keep controlled temporal interventions supplementary: remove matched newest/oldest counts, shuffle earlier items while retaining the last item, and shuffle the entire history using fixed repeated permutations and unchanged validation candidates. Report paired hit, target-rank, and score changes with explicit tie handling. Frequency-matched replacements can help assess popularity confounding. These are inference-reliance probes; they do not establish causal intent or retrained ablation performance.

For uncertainty, run 10,000 seed-42 paired bootstrap replicates, independently resampling validation users within each category while using identical indices for compared models and averaging the four category differences equally. Keep each user's candidate set intact. Label the observed difference and percentile interval exploratory: the interval is conditional on trained models and candidates and does not adjust for winner selection, training seeds, or negative-sampling variability. Do not create new splits or access held-out test outcomes during search.

Preserve DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], all four categories, dataset routing, single-GPU execution, and artifacts beneath the trial directory. Update the predictor writer to serialize/load CSR counts, popularity, tau, scales, correction type, shared alpha, routing, and fallback rules. Check loaded-versus-training scorer parity on fixed training histories and candidates, including sparse rows, empty histories, padding, and candidate batches. Available metadata consists only of public titles, descriptions, and timestamps; do not consume the generic input's unavailable ratings, reviews, categories, prices, or stores. For the twenty training users, catalog coverage, popularity, concentration, and evidence-qualified simulator judgments remain supplementary and cannot establish relevance or latent diversity/conformity. No benchmark gain has been measured.
idea_diagnosis.pseudocode:
for category in four_categories:
    fit unchanged SASRec using prescribed split, seeds, and epoch environment
    C = CSR adjacent-transition counts from nonpadding training histories
    n = row_sums(C)
    p = add_one_smoothed_training_occurrence_popularity()
    tau = 20
    residual(i,j) = (C[i,j] - n[i]*p[j]) / (n[i] + tau)
    training_pairs = sample_training_prefix_candidates(seed=42, count=10000)
    sigma_s = max(population_std(neural_scores(training_pairs)), 1e-8)
    rms_r = max(root_mean_square(residual_scores(training_pairs)), 1e-8)
    save counts, p, tau, scales, routing, fallback rules
for alpha in [0, .25, .5, .75, 1]:
    score(h,j) = neural(h,j)/sigma_s + alpha*residual(last_nonpadding(h),j)/rms_r
    empty_history_score(j) = p[j]
    obtain pinned validation hits without changing candidates or tie handling
    save every user's hit and category score
select shared alpha by four-category macro HR@10; prefer smaller alpha on ties
write predictor using the same scorer and serialized artifacts
verify scorer parity on fixed training-only examples
run prespecified supplementary controls, support strata, and temporal probes within budget
report paired stratified bootstrap interval as descriptive and selection-unadjusted
restore model mode after every diagnostic probe

originality.negative: Transition counts, shrinkage, popularity corrections, additive ensembles, and their ablations are established methods; the contribution is primarily experimental integration.

future_potential.positive: An inexpensive, falsifiable test can determine whether local pairwise evidence adds value and motivate controlled history-aware extensions.
future_potential.negative: Sparse support, popularity shortcuts, and validation selection may explain apparent gains; the method cannot infer purpose, compatibility, or current demand.

code_difficulty.positive: The primary branch requires sparse counts and additive scoring without retraining a new architecture or fetching external resources.
code_difficulty.negative: Training-fixed calibration, efficient catalog scoring, diagnostic source alignment, reproducible controls, and predictor serialization substantially exceed the difficulty of the scoring formula alone.

  - Official SASRec positional encoding: positions 0..maxlen-1 with padding masked after dropout
  - Official PointWiseFeedForward: Conv1d → Dropout → ReLU → Conv1d → Dropout + residual
  - Official BCEWithLogits loss on positive and negative sequence logits
  - Early stopping with patience=20 (checked every 5 epochs)
  - Writes predict.py routing to per-dataset models via dataset_name kwarg

Key hyper-parameters (all tunable by RecHarness):
  HIDDEN_UNITS : embedding / attention dimension
  NUM_BLOCKS   : number of self-attention blocks
  NUM_HEADS    : number of attention heads
  DROPOUT_RATE : dropout on attention + FFN
  LR           : Adam learning rate
  WEIGHT_DECAY : Adam weight decay
  BATCH_SIZE   : training batch size
  NUM_BATCHES  : gradient steps per epoch

        raise ValueError("Dataset has no training histories with two items")
    batch_seq, batch_pos, batch_neg = [], [], []
    for _ in range(batch_size):
        history = user_train[random.choice(users)]
        seq = np.zeros(maxlen, dtype=np.int32)
        pos = np.zeros(maxlen, dtype=np.int32)
        neg = np.zeros(maxlen, dtype=np.int32)
        nxt = history[-1]
        idx = maxlen - 1
        ts = set(history) if sample_negatives else set()
        can_sample = sample_negatives and len(ts) < itemnum
        for item in reversed(history[:-1]):
            seq[idx] = item
            pos[idx] = nxt

                    neg_item = random.randint(1, itemnum)
                neg[idx] = neg_item
            nxt = item
            idx -= 1
            if idx == -1:
                break

        batch_pos.append(pos)
        batch_neg.append(neg)
    return np.array(batch_seq), np.array(batch_pos), np.array(batch_neg)


@torch.no_grad()
def sample_causal_candidates(
    seq: torch.Tensor, positive: torch.Tensor, itemnum: int, count: int = 32
):
    """Uniform replacement draws excluding only the visible prefix and target.

    Stable sorting makes the first matching item carry its earliest position.
    Thus membership tests do not exclude items occurring only in later positions.
    No quadratic catalog mask or B x L x K x L tensor is constructed.
    """
    batch, length = seq.shape
    positions = torch.arange(length, device=seq.device).unsqueeze(0)
    sorted_items, original_positions = torch.sort(seq, dim=1, stable=True)

    def first_occurrence(values):
        shape = values.shape
        flat = values.reshape(batch, -1).contiguous()
        index = torch.searchsorted(sorted_items.contiguous(), flat)
        index = index.clamp_max(length - 1)
        found = sorted_items.gather(1, index).eq(flat)
        first = original_positions.gather(1, index)
        return found.reshape(shape), first.reshape(shape)

    _, first_input = first_occurrence(seq)
    unique_prefix_count = (seq.ne(0) & first_input.eq(positions)).long().cumsum(1)
    found_target, first_target = first_occurrence(positive)
    target_in_prefix = found_target & first_target.le(positions)
    available = itemnum - unique_prefix_count - (~target_in_prefix).long()
    valid = seq.ne(0) & positive.ne(0)
    eligible = valid & available.gt(0)
    skipped = (valid & ~eligible).sum()
    negatives = torch.randint(1, itemnum + 1, (batch, length, count), device=seq.device)

    def rejected(draws):
        found, first = first_occurrence(draws)
        prefix_hit = found & first.le(positions.unsqueeze(-1))
        return (prefix_hit | draws.eq(positive.unsqueeze(-1))) & eligible.unsqueeze(-1)

    bad = rejected(negatives)
    for _ in range(8):
        number_bad = int(bad.sum().item())
        if number_bad == 0:

        negatives[bad] = torch.randint(1, itemnum + 1, (number_bad,), device=seq.device)

    # Both accepted rejection draws and fallback draws are uniform on A.
    if bool(bad.any().item()):

            n = int(mask.sum().item())
            indices = torch.randint(allowed.numel(), (n,), device=seq.device)
            negatives[b, t, mask] = allowed[indices]
    return negatives, eligible, skipped


def candidate_cross_entropy(model, features, positive, negatives, chunk_size=1024):

    from torch.utils.checkpoint import checkpoint

    if features.shape[0] == 0:
        raise ValueError("Candidate CE requires at least one eligible position")

        positive_embeddings = nn.functional.embedding(positive_chunk, item_weight)
        negative_embeddings = nn.functional.embedding(negative_chunk, item_weight)
        positive_score = (feature_chunk * positive_embeddings).sum(-1, keepdim=True)
        negative_score = torch.einsum("nd,nkd->nk", feature_chunk, negative_embeddings)
        logits = torch.cat((positive_score, negative_score), dim=-1)
        labels = torch.zeros(logits.shape[0], dtype=torch.long, device=logits.device)
        return nn.functional.cross_entropy(logits, labels, reduction="sum")

    total = features.new_zeros(())
    for start in range(0, features.shape[0], chunk_size):

            chunk_loss,
            features[start:stop],
            positive[start:stop],
            negatives[start:stop],
            model.item_emb.weight,
            use_reentrant=False,
            preserve_rng_state=False,

    return total / features.shape[0]

def evaluate_val(
    model: SASRec,
    user_train: dict,
    user_valid: dict,
    itemnum: int,
    device: torch.device,
    maxlen: int = 128,
    num_users: int = 200,
) -> dict[str, float]:
    ### >>> Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-START: Deterministic validation without resetting training RNG
    rng = random.Random(42)
    val_users = [u for u in user_valid if u in user_train and user_valid[u]]
    if len(val_users) > num_users:
        val_users = rng.sample(val_users, num_users)
    ### <<< Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-END

    HR10 = HR20 = NDCG10 = NDCG20 = 0.0
    model.eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        for u in val_users:
            pos_items = user_valid[u]
            if not pos_items:
                continue
            target = pos_items[0]

            hist = user_train[u][-maxlen:]
            seq_arr = np.zeros(maxlen, dtype=np.int32)
            for i, item in enumerate(reversed(hist)):
                seq_arr[maxlen - 1 - i] = item

            seq_t = torch.tensor(seq_arr, dtype=torch.long, device=device).unsqueeze(0)
            neg_pool: set[int] = set()
            interacted = set(user_train[u]) | set(pos_items)
            ### >>> Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-START: Keep validation candidates unique and locally seeded
            if itemnum - len(interacted) < 99:
                raise ValueError("Validation requires 99 unique unseen candidates")
            while len(neg_pool) < 99:
                ni = rng.randint(1, itemnum)
                if ni not in interacted:
                    neg_pool.add(ni)
            ### <<< Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-END
            candidates = [target] + list(neg_pool)

            cand_t = torch.tensor([candidates], dtype=torch.long, device=device)
            scores = model.predict(seq_t, cand_t)[0].cpu().numpy().tolist()
            rank = sorted(range(len(candidates)), key=lambda i: -scores[i]).index(0)

            HR10 += 1.0 if rank < 10 else 0.0
            HR20 += 1.0 if rank < 20 else 0.0
            NDCG10 += (1.0 / math.log2(rank + 2)) if rank < 10 else 0.0
            NDCG20 += (1.0 / math.log2(rank + 2)) if rank < 20 else 0.0

    n = max(len(val_users), 1)
    model.train()
    return {
        "HR@10": HR10 / n,
        "HR@20": HR20 / n,
        "NDCG@10": NDCG10 / n,
        "NDCG@20": NDCG20 / n,
    }

            "sampled_embeddings": int(count),
            "usable_embeddings": 0,
            "excluded_embeddings": 0,
        }
        if count == 0:
            return None
        rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
        indices = torch.as_tensor(
            rng.choice(emb.shape[0], count, replace=False),
            dtype=torch.long,
            device=emb.device,
        )
        # Convert before computing norms: float32 norms can overflow or underflow.
        sampled = emb.index_select(0, indices).double()
        norms = sampled.norm(dim=-1)
        usable = torch.isfinite(sampled).all(-1) & torch.isfinite(norms) & norms.gt(0)
        self.embedding_observation_counts = {
            "catalog_nonpadding_embeddings": int(emb.shape[0]),
            "sampled_embeddings": int(count),
            "usable_embeddings": int(usable.sum().item()),
            "excluded_embeddings": int((~usable).sum().item()),
        }
        sampled = sampled[usable]
        count = sampled.shape[0]
        if count < 2:
            return None
        x = sampled / norms[usable].unsqueeze(-1)
        # Sum of off-diagonal dot products without a quadratic Gram matrix.
        total = x.sum(0).square().sum() - x.square().sum()
        mean_cosine = (total / (count * (count - 1))).clamp(-1, 1)
        return float(((mean_cosine + 1) / 2).item())

    @staticmethod
    def _summarize(chunks, eps):
        names = ("mean", "p10", "neg_beats_pos_rate", "small_margin_rate", "tie_rate")
        if not chunks:
            return dict.fromkeys(names, None)
        margins = torch.cat(chunks)
        k = max(1, int(np.ceil(0.10 * margins.numel())))
        return {
            "mean": float(margins.mean().item()),
            "p10": float(margins.kthvalue(k).values.item()),
            "neg_beats_pos_rate": float((margins < 0).double().mean().item()),
            "small_margin_rate": float((margins < eps).double().mean().item()),
            "tie_rate": float((margins == 0).double().mean().item()),
        }

    @torch.no_grad()
    def analyze_pos_neg_margin_with_category_breakdown(
        self, dataloader, num_batches=10, eps=0.5, topk_categories=20
    ):
        from itertools import islice

        if not np.isfinite(float(eps)):
            raise ValueError("Diagnostic margin threshold must be finite")
        # Iterating a training loader can consume global RNG state even in eval mode.
        # Restore the RNGs used by this single-device workflow on success or failure.
        python_rng = random.getstate()
        numpy_rng = np.random.get_state()
        torch_rng = torch.random.get_rng_state()
        cuda_rng = (
            torch.cuda.get_rng_state(self.device)
            if self.device.type == "cuda"
            else None
        )
        chunks = {"neural": [], "deployed": []}
        counts = {
            "batches": 0,
            "valid_positions": 0,
            "neural_finite_positions": 0,
            "deployed_finite_positions": 0,
            "neural_nonfinite_positions": 0,
            "deployed_nonfinite_positions": 0,
        }
        # Preserve mixed submodule modes too, including when scoring raises.
        modes = [(module, module.training) for module in self.model.modules()]
        try:
            self.model.eval()
            for batch in islice(dataloader, max(int(num_batches), 0)):
                if not isinstance(batch, (list, tuple)) or len(batch) != 4:
                    raise ValueError("Expected (None, sequence, positive, negative)")
                seq, pos, neg = [
                    torch.as_tensor(value, dtype=torch.long, device=self.device)
                    for value in batch[1:]
                ]
                if seq.ndim != 2 or pos.shape != seq.shape or neg.shape != seq.shape:
                    raise ValueError(
                        "Diagnostic sequence, positive and negative must be B x L"
                    )
                counts["batches"] += 1
                valid = seq.ne(0) & pos.ne(0) & neg.ne(0)
                counts["valid_positions"] += int(valid.sum().item())
                if not bool(valid.any().item()):
                    continue
                features = self.view.log2feats(seq)
                if (
                    not isinstance(features, torch.Tensor)
                    or features.ndim != 3
                    or features.shape[:2] != seq.shape
                ):
                    raise ValueError("view.log2feats must return B x L x D features")
                items = torch.stack((pos, neg), dim=-1)
                scorers = [("neural", self.view.predict_score)]
                if self.deployed_score is not None:
                    scorers.append(("deployed", self.deployed_score))
                for scope, scorer in scorers:
                    if scope == "deployed":
                        # At t the causal feature predicts positive[:, t] from seq[:, t].
                        logits = scorer(features, items, seq)
                    else:
                        logits = scorer(features, items)
                    if logits.shape != items.shape:
                        raise ValueError(f"{scope} scorer must return B x L x 2")
                    finite = torch.isfinite(logits).all(dim=-1)
                    usable = valid & finite
                    counts[f"{scope}_finite_positions"] += int(usable.sum().item())
                    counts[f"{scope}_nonfinite_positions"] += int(
                        (valid & ~finite).sum().item()
                    )
                    if bool(usable.any().item()):
                        selected = logits[usable].detach().double()
                        chunks[scope].append((selected[:, 0] - selected[:, 1]).cpu())
        finally:
            for module, training in modes:
                module.training = training
            random.setstate(python_rng)
            np.random.set_state(numpy_rng)
            torch.random.set_rng_state(torch_rng)
            if cuda_rng is not None:
                torch.cuda.set_rng_state(cuda_rng, self.device)

        neural = self._summarize(chunks["neural"], float(eps))
        breakdown = {
            "eps": float(eps),
            "observation_counts": counts,
            "deployed_available": self.deployed_score is not None,
            "deployed_margins": self._summarize(chunks["deployed"], float(eps)),
            "category_breakdown": None,
            "category_breakdown_reason": "Item categories are unavailable in this task.",
        }
        return neural, breakdown
